hints: In a sorted list, which element has the same number of values on each side? That element is a good root.
Use divide and conquer on index ranges. The middle index (lo + hi) / 2 becomes the node, and the two halves become its left and right subtrees, built the same way.

1. build(lo, hi): if lo > hi, return null.
  2. Set mid = (lo + hi) / 2, rounded down.
  3. Create a node with nums[mid].
  4. Set left = build(lo, mid−1) and right = build(mid+1, hi).
  5. Return the node.

approaches.name: Brute force (copy halves)
approaches.idea: Use the same recursion, but copy the left and right halves into new arrays at each level.

approaches.name: Optimal (index ranges)
approaches.idea: Recurse on lo/hi indices with no copying. Each element becomes exactly one node.

explain: For [-8,-1,0,4,11], mid = 2, so 0 is the root. The left half [-8,-1] has mid = (0+1)/2 = 0, so -8 is the root there and -1 becomes its right child. The right half [4,11] likewise gives 4 with 11 on its right. The result is [0,-8,4,null,-1,null,11]. The tree is a BST because everything left of mid is smaller and everything right of it is larger. It is balanced because the two halves differ in size by at most one. The rule says to round down, so for two elements the left one is the root (sample 2: 2 with right child 6).
recognize: When a sorted array must become a balanced BST, pick the middle as the root and recurse on each half.
